title: Daemon identification — argv/start-time identity on the Hermes Stop path
scope: Rust unit and integration tests with isolated, owned subprocesses. No daemon signal or runtime PID-state mutation outside those owned children.

implemented.shared_module: services/agentbox-ops/src/process_identity.rs (new) factors the reaper argv-allowlist and start-time logic into one documented module, now used by the Hermes Stop path.
implemented.identity_before_signal: Before signalling, the target PID must match BOTH the recorded argv (/proc/<pid>/cmdline) and the recorded start time (/proc/<pid>/stat field 22). Both are captured at launch into the job record (hermes/jobs.rs); a record lacking them is UNVERIFIABLE and refuses to signal rather than guessing.
implemented.staleness_recheck: Identity is re-checked immediately before the signal, not at plan time.
implemented.delivery_vs_shutdown: SIGTERM delivery and confirmed shutdown are reported separately: after the signal a bounded grace period re-checks identity, yielding distinct outcomes for confirmed-exited, signalled-but-still-running, identity-mismatch-refused and no-such-process. Missing /proc access is an explicit refusal, never an assumed match. Recoverable state is preserved on failure.
implemented.reaper_default: The reaper stays read-only by default, asserted by tests/reaper_default_is_read_only.rs.
